catalogue_claim.text: Proves that sufficiently close unital von Neumann algebras on the same Hilbert space are conjugate by a unitary arbitrarily close to the identity, with a universal tolerance in the operator-norm distance between unit balls. Counterexamples show that near-identity conjugacy fails for one-sided near inclusions, and that arbitrarily close norm-separable C∗-algebras need not be ambiently unitarily conjugate. ([Lean](lean/docs/289.md))

statements.section_title: Introduction
statements.text:
\label{thm:main}
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are a separable complex Hilbert space $H$
and unital, norm-separable $C^*$-algebras $A,B\subseteq\B(H)$ with common
identity $\id_H$ such that
\[
\KK(A,B)<\varepsilon,\qquad A''=B'',
\]
but no unitary $u\in\B(H)$ satisfies $uAu^*=B$.

statements.section_title: Introduction
statements.text:
\label{thm:main}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $\delta=\delta(\eps)>0$ such that the
following holds. If $H$ is any complex Hilbert space and
$M,N\subseteq\B(H)$ are unital von Neumann algebras with identity
$I_H$ and $d(M,N)<\delta$, there is a unitary $u\in\B(H)$ satisfying
\[
 uMu^*=N,\qquad \norm{u-I_H}<\eps.
\]
